agent_summary: IL-10/TNF is not a gap: 5 independent canine units compared IL-10 or TNF by severity or outcome (CH03, CB037, CH23, CB109, CH37). No dog study reported the IL-10/TNF ratio itself; DS02 has both cytokines. Soluble CD14 (CB112, complicated > uncomplicated, which is DS07 itself) and suPAR (CB004, complicated vs uncomplicated B. canis, no difference) are also already severity-tested. The real gaps are regulatory T cells / PD-1 (never measured in canine babesiosis; CB008 measured only CD3/CD4/CD8/B cells), monocyte DLA class II (only whole-blood transcripts in CB082/DS06), soluble TREM-1 (no canine soluble assay found) and complement factor H (added; only in proteomics, CB019 pools and DS07 master A0A5F4BVG1, never reported by severity). One surprise: the DS07 factor H masters are labelled 'Uncharacterized protein ... GN=CFH', so a description-prefix match on 'Complement factor H' will miss them; match on GN=CFH.

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS02 IL-10 and TNF-alpha (5 experimental Beagles; ratio computable); DS06 IL10 and TNF gene expression (whole-blood RNA, not circulating protein); not in DS07
mechanisms.notes: Units: CH03, CB037, CH23, CB109 (mRNA), CH37 (TNF correlations only). Only CB037 measured both IL-10 and TNF in one severity contrast; no dog study reported the IL-10/TNF ratio, so the ratio is a narrow sub-gap that DS02 can address descriptively. Results mixed: IL-10 raised by infection but not by outcome in CH03 or CH23 (SV-04).

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 master A0A5F4BVG1 (GN=CFH, 15% coverage; described as 'Uncharacterized protein', so match on GN=CFH, not the description) plus master candidates E2RK21, A0A5F4CHF6, J9NTL7, A0A5F4CLV4, A0A5F4BYC6; DS06 CFH not checked by reference_lookup; not in DS02
mechanisms.notes: Measured in dogs only by mass spectrometry; no canine factor H immunoassay found. CB112's global test implicitly covered factor H but reported nothing, so an explicit DS07 test (part b) would be the first severity contrast. Human evidence comes from one Gambian group (two papers, overlapping children) plus a Ghanaian FHR-1 genetic cohort.
